question.problem: The intensity of radiation $I,$ in milliroentgen/hour ($\text{mR}/\text{h}$), spreading out from an X-ray device is inversely proportional to the **square** of the distance $d,$ measured in meters, between the device and the object being radiated. If a device that measures the radiation intensity registers $82\,\text{mR}/\text{h}$ at a distance of $5\,\text{m}.$ What equation gives the relationship between $I$ and $d?$
question.worked_solution:
Since the intensity $I$ is inversely proportional to the square of the distance $d,$ we must have

$$
I=\frac{k}{{d}^{2}},
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that $82\,\text{mR}/\text{h}$ when $d=5\,\text{m}.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}82 & =\frac{k}{{5}^{2}} \\ 82 & =\frac{k}{25} \\ 82\cdot 25 & =k \\ 2\,050 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our inverse variation equation is

$$
I=\frac{2\,050}{{d}^{2}}.
$$
